rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken word for a train as a rail vehicle.

example.english: I take the train to work every day.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat6 jat6 daap3 fo2 ce1 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this formal term for a coupled carriage set or for a railway train in official contexts.

example.english: Please note that the train is about to depart.
example.jyutping: cing2 lau4 ji3 lit6 ce1 zik1 zoeng1 hoi1 ceot1

rows.note: Use 訓練 for deliberately developing someone’s ability through practice or conditioning.

example.english: We train with the coach every morning.
example.traditional: 我哋每日朝早跟教練訓練。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 mui5 jat6 ziu1 zou2 gan1 gaau3 lin6 fan3 lin6

rows.note: Use 教 for the teaching or educating aspect of training someone, rather than the conditioning aspect.

example.english: I train my son to play soccer.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gaau3 go3 zai2 tek3 bo1

rows.note: Use 練習 as the all-purpose verb for practising an ability or skill.

example.english: I train by swimming every day.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 lin6 zaap6 jau4 seoi2

rows.note: Use 健身 when working out specifically to improve physical fitness.

example.english: I train at the gym after work.
example.jyutping: ngo5 fong3 gung1 zi1 hau6 heoi3 gin6 san1

rows.note: Use this for the ideas or reasoning in a train of thought.

example.english: Explain your train of thought more clearly first.
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 cing1 co2 di1 si1 lou6 sin1

rows.note: Use this for a linked sequence of events rather than a train of thoughts.

example.english: This train of events is truly shocking.
example.traditional: 呢一連串事件真係令人震驚。
example.jyutping: ni1 jat1 lin4 cyun3 si6 gin6 zan1 hai6 ling6 jan4 zan3 ging1
